This draft uses 199 sheets, compared with the initial 150-sheet allowance. The layout preserves all flat grey profiles and uses upright tower panels. It is a conservative rectangular nest; tighter use of irregular offcuts could reduce the count before the fixed quotation.

Façade overview. Separate physical layers are overlaid in this review image. Pale lines show proposed panel joins.

Production files are released after payment.

This page contains review previews and the budget breakdown. The cutting files, detailed sheet nests, full-size drawings and production assets are held for the paid handover.

Vertical tower panels

The outer towers use 900 × 2380 mm main modules with a 100 mm top closure behind the crown. Inner towers use 900 × 2250 mm modules. Centre piers use approximately 813 × 2275 mm modules. Banner trim uses upright sections.

Mirrored partners share matching seam heights and reflected vertical divisions. Centre sections divide symmetrically about the stage centreline. Spires use two equal-height sections, and the small finials split down their centre.

Before the final cutting price

The draft keeps a 10 mm stock-edge margin and 10 mm between profiles. The proposed seams, backing, fixings, plywood grade and 9 mm thickness need to be agreed with the stage designer before machining.

The scope covers the flat grey façade only. The dragon body, backing battens, splice plates, additional structural parts, finishing and installation are separate.

Preliminary design and production programmeThese are proposed panel joins for review. The design is still being finalised, and the quoted sheet quantity, machining time and completion date remain subject to the approved production design and a confirmed workshop slot.

Why a range?

Long, open profiles should run more quickly than dense nests with many small features. The final split lines, cut length, hold-down method and nesting will determine the actual cycle time.

For budgeting, the calculated lower total is rounded down and the upper total rounded up to the nearest $500. Preparation stays at 6–10 hours in these quantity scenarios; major rework or a substantially different part count needs a new estimate.

Read the rate and estimating basis

The $120/hour CNC rate is taken from Create Wonder's Aperion invoice 2026-0111 dated 12 January 2026, as confirmed for this estimate. That invoice covered a smaller half-sheet job. Its total and runtime have not been scaled to price the mainstage.

The 20–30 minute full-sheet cycle, 6–10 preparation hours, bit life, waste allowance and 10% design reserve are new estimating assumptions. The $30 bit allowance is also consistent with the January reference. No completed nesting or CAM simulation is claimed.

A clear cutting scope.

This budget covers the sheet-cutting service. Aperion supplies the plywood and retains responsibility for the stage design and assembly.

Included in the allowance

  • Review and preparation of final 2D cutting files, nesting and toolpaths.
  • CNC profile cutting of the supplied 9 mm plywood, sheet changeovers and basic part identification.
  • Router tooling and a provisional allowance for machining waste disposal.
  • A 10% budget reserve for minor changes while the current design is developed.

To be priced separately if required

  • Plywood procurement, inbound transport, delivery and special packaging.
  • Major revisions to this proposed panelisation, extra backing parts or additional unlisted profiles.
  • Sanding, paint, flame-retardant treatment, assembly, framing and installation.
  • 3D carving of the dragon, printed graphics, lighting, hardware and structural engineering.
Before the fixed quoteConfirm the 9 mm plywood grade and approve the proposed seams, seam backing, part quantities and joint details with the stage designer.
